title: Worry eats away
odia:
ଚିନ୍ତା ଖାଏ ଗଣ୍ଡି
ଲୁଣ ଖାଏ ହାଣ୍ଡି।
literal_meaning: Worry eats the body; salt eats the pot.
meaning_odia: ଚିନ୍ତା ଦେହକୁ ଖାଏ, ଲୁଣ ହାଣ୍ଡିକୁ ଖାଏ—ଦୁଇ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଏକେ କ୍ରିୟାର ତୁଳନା ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଲଗାତାର ଚିନ୍ତାରେ ମଣିଷ ଭିତରୁ କ୍ଷୟ ହେଉଥିବା ପରି ଅନୁଭବ କରିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଧରିଛି। ଏହା ଚିନ୍ତାର ଭାରକୁ ବୁଝାଉଥିବା ରୂପକ।
explanation: The same verb, eats, gives worry and salt a consuming force: one acts on the body, the other on the pot. Read editorially, the comparison conveys the feeling of being worn down by persistent worry. Its strength lies in making an inward burden visible through a familiar household object.
usage_example: Original imagined example: After days of turning the same unresolved matter over in their mind, someone quotes the couplet to describe how worn down they feel.
cultural_context: ଗଣ୍ଡି and ହାଣ୍ଡି rhyme, while ଖାଏ repeats in the same position in both lines. That parallel gives the body and the pot matching places in the comparison.

english_summary: Worry is pictured as eating a person away.
